title: Embedding quantization: automated recalibration and cosine-drift detection playbook (FP8/INT8/FP16)
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Purpose: Define and implement an operational playbook for (1) producing and validating embedding quantization profiles across FP8/INT8/FP16 variants and (2) detecting and remediating cosine-similarity drift in production embeddings. This ticket bundles the calibration harness, reproducible evaluation protocol, CI gating, monitoring alerts, and an automated recalibration trigger with safe rollout and rollback behavior.

Background: We have multiple experimental and production embedding models served in hosted and dedicated modes. Past audits (see ENG-18940 and ENG-15823) showed occasional cosine-similarity regressions after changing kernel selection or applying aggressive quantization. Teams need a reliable, automated pipeline so that: (a) quantized variants meet quality SLAs vs FP32 baseline, (b) regressions are detected quickly in prod, and (c) recalibration can be executed safely with minimal customer disruption.

Goals:
- Produce per-model quantization profiles (scale/zero-point/clip) for INT8 and FP8 candidates, and a calibration-preserving FP16 profile for lower-cost hosts.
- Define acceptance criteria (mean cosine drop, 90th percentile drop, and statistically significant regression tests) relative to an FP32 baseline.
- Implement an automated calibration workflow (offline calibration -> CI validation -> canary rollout -> monitor & auto-promote/rollback).
- Build monitoring and alerting (cosine drift detector, baseline-change detector, and calibration staleness metric).
- Provide runbooks and a safe ops interface to trigger recalibration or rollbacks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration harness outputs profiles and a standardized csv artifact: model, variant, quant_scheme, sample_count, mean_cosine, median_cosine, p_value_bootstrap, psa_delta_90.
- For any model, the INT8/FP8 variant passes: mean cosine drop <= 0.012 and 95th-percentile drop <= 0.04 OR p_value_bootstrap > 0.05 (no statistically significant regression). FP16 must be within mean drop <= 0.005.
evaluation_plan:
Dataset: Use curated validation bank of 50k representative pairs: 30k near-duplicate pairs, 15k semantic-similar, 5k random negatives. Each pair includes provenance (product, region, language). Keep a frozen canonical sample in GCS: gs://redwood-embeddings/quant/calibration-banks/v3/50k.csv.

Metrics: cosine_mean_delta, cosine_median_delta, delta_pctl_90, bootstrap_p_value (10k bootstrap iterations), AUC for ranking tasks. Compute confidence intervals and per-segment stratified stats (by length, domain, confidence).

Protocol:
1) Offline calibration job (calibration-worker) runs quant sweep: {INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric, FP8-e4m3, FP8-e5m2, FP16 fallback}.
2) For each candidate profile, run eval harness to compute metrics vs FP32 baseline.
3) Reject variants not meeting acceptance criteria.
4) Store artifact in MLArtifacts store with semantic versioning.
5) CI gate (PR) fails if candidate causes any per-segment mean_drop > 0.02 or p_value_bootstrap < 0.01.

Reproducibility: Use deterministic seeds and recorded commit hashes for compiler/kernels. Include bit-identical runs with fixed kernel overrides where applicable. Save RNG seed in artifact metadata.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: 2% traffic for 24 hours with detailed telemetry.
- If canary mean_delta <= acceptance and no alert fired, ramp to 20% for 12 hours, then to 100% with gradual increments.
- Auto-rollback triggers: sustained mean_delta > 0.02 for 30m or >0.04 for any 5m window, or error rate > baseline + 0.5pp.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- New metric: embedding.quant.cosine_delta. TTL-based baseline window: rolling 7d baseline updated daily.
- Alert thresholds: P0 alert on mean_delta > 0.02 (severity: PagerDuty), P1 on p_value_bootstrap < 0.01.
- Dashboard: per-model/time-window distributions, per-segment breakdowns, and canary vs baseline comparisons.

Automation:
- A scheduled job (weekly) computes calibration_staleness: days_since_last_calibration. If >30 days AND traffic pattern changed (KL divergence > 0.03), mark for auto-recalibration review.
- Automated recalibration job requires a green CI run and an Ops approval step (1-click in Console) prior to canary. Option to enable fully-automated mode for low-risk internal models.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- FP8: we will evaluate two FP8 formats (e4m3 and e5m2) — e4m3 has smaller dynamic range and slightly lower median cosine; e5m2 may preserve tail similarity better but has larger hardware variance depending on kernel. We'll prefer e5m2 for semantic-heavy models unless calibration cost outweighs benefits.
- INT8 symmetric quant performs best for short sequences but requires zero-point handling for odd tokenizations; asymmetric reduces bias but increases storage/compute.
- Calibration cost: large calibration banks (50k) give stability but increase job time. We will run fast 5k sanity sweeps for CI and full 50k nightly jobs.

Artifacts and links:
- Calibration harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibration-harness (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibration-harness/pull/72)
- Eval notebook (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_calib_eval_v3
- Canonical dataset: gs://redwood-embeddings/quant/calibration-banks/v3/50k.csv
- Example CI job: https://ci.redwood.com/jobs/quant-eval/12345

Security/Privacy: All calibration datasets must use anonymized user ids and only include public or opt-in telemetry. See privacy playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/privacy/embedding-data-guidelines.

notes_for_reviewers:
Please focus reviews on: (a) acceptance thresholds (mean delta bounds and bootstrap parameters), (b) proposed rollout %/timings, and (c) monitoring definitions. If you have historical incidents with false-positive drift alerts, include those examples in PR comments so we can tune thresholds.

Key open question: Should we allow model owners to opt-in to fully-automated recalibration for non-customer-facing internal models? Pros: reduces manual toil. Cons: risk of automated changes without human oversight. Suggest opt-in with audit logs by default.
